issues.legal_issue: A request to convert an existing leasehold into freehold by paying the amount fixed for transfer of the remaining ownership rights is not a consumer service, so a consumer forum lacks jurisdiction over a complaint alleging deficient service in that conversion.
material_facts: The applicants already held plots on lease and sought freehold title by paying conversion amounts fixed by the administration.
The government retained ownership until the consideration for transfer was paid in full.
The conversion amount was part of the consideration for transfer of title, not a charge for a service rendered to the applicants.
The complaints concerned the transfer of title, not deficient housing construction or another service.
issues.conclusion: The administration was not providing a consumer service by converting leasehold plots to freehold, and the consumer fora lacked jurisdiction over the complaints. The orders of the consumer fora were set aside.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 2(d), 2(g), 2(o) and 14(e) of the Consumer Protection Act, 1986, a consumer complaint requires a service hired or availed of and an alleged deficiency in that service. Section 3 of the Capital of Punjab (Development and Regulation) Act, 1952 and the applicable lease and conversion rules showed that the conversion payment was consideration for transferring the remaining title. Lucknow Development Authority v. M.K. Gupta and Ghaziabad Development Authority v. Balbir Singh recognize consumer jurisdiction over deficiencies in services rendered by statutory authorities, including housing construction; they do not make a transfer of title a service. Chandigarh Housing Board v. Avtar Singh was also considered. The Court applied UT Chandigarh Administration v. Amarjeet Singh, which held that a public auction of existing sites does not involve a consumer service, and distinguished cases involving housing services from a sale of immovable property.

rule.if: consumer_complaint_concerns_conversion and existing_leasehold_rights and conversion_payment_is_purchase_consideration and no_service_is_rendered

predicates.consumer_complaint_concerns_conversion: A consumer complaint alleges deficient service in the conversion of a property from leasehold to freehold.
predicates.existing_leasehold_rights: The complainant already holds the property under leasehold rights.
predicates.conversion_payment_is_purchase_considera: The payment sought for conversion is consideration for acquiring the remaining ownership rights.
predicates.no_service_is_rendered: The authority transfers title without rendering a separate service to the applicant.

issues.definition: When a consumer complaint concerns conversion of an existing leasehold, the payment buys the remaining ownership rights, and no separate service is rendered, the consumer forum lacks jurisdiction.

issues.legal_issue: A notation in a government file does not become a binding government order unless it is finalized and communicated to the person affected.
material_facts: The consumer fora relied on a notation by an administrator stating that no decision would be taken until clear directions were received from the central government.
The notation was an internal part of the decision-making process and was not shown to have been communicated as a final order to the affected applicants.
issues.conclusion: The internal notation could not, by itself, support a finding of deficiency in service or be treated as a binding government order.
issues.legal_principle: In Bachhittar Singh v. State of Punjab, relying also on State of Punjab v. Sodhi Sukhdev Singh, the Court held that an internal file opinion remains provisional until a final decision is made and communicated to the affected person. The judgment applied that principle to the notation relied on by the consumer fora.

predicates.government_order_status_is_in_issue: A party relies on an internal government notation as though it were a final government decision.
predicates.only_internal_file_notation_exists: The asserted decision appears only as a notation in an administrative file.
predicates.notation_was_not_communicated: The notation was not communicated to the person affected as a final order.

issues.definition: When only an uncommunicated internal notation is relied on as a government decision, it is not a binding order.

issues.legal_issue: An administration cannot keep conversion applications pending merely because it is considering revising charges while the governing conversion scheme remains in force.
material_facts: The governing conversion rules remained in force when the applications were made and while they were pending.
An administrative communication directed that conversions stop while revised rates were under consideration.
The applications were kept pending because of the anticipated revision of conversion charges, and the rates were revised only later.
The Court directed the administration to decide the conversion claims by reference to the date the consumer complaints were filed.
issues.conclusion: The administrative pause could not displace the rules or justify keeping the applications pending; the action was arbitrary and discriminatory. The administration was directed to decide the conversion claims as of the date the consumer complaints were filed.
issues.legal_principle: The statutory conversion rules remained operative and could not be suspended by an administrative communication issued while a rate revision was under consideration. The Court characterized the refusal to decide the applications on that basis as arbitrary and discriminatory and, exercising its power under Article 142 of the Constitution, directed the administration to decide the claims as of the complaint-filing date.

predicates.conversion_complaint_case: The matter concerns a consumer complaint seeking conversion of an existing leasehold property to freehold.
predicates.conversion_scheme_remained_in_force: The governing conversion scheme remained in force while the applications were pending.
predicates.applications_were_held_for_rate_revision: The administration kept the applications pending because it was considering revising the conversion charges.

issues.definition: When a conversion complaint concerns applications held for a rate revision while the conversion scheme remains in force, the administration must decide the claims by reference to the complaint-filing date.
